## Observations

1. Every valid result is an even-length prefix of the infinite pattern `ioioio…`. Insertions preserve the order of the original characters, so the goal is to find the shortest such prefix containing `S` as a subsequence.
2. Matching each original character to its earliest available position leaves at least as much room for the remaining characters as any later match. In the alternating pattern, a match needs no insertion if the next expected character agrees, and exactly one insertion otherwise.
3. After all original characters are matched, an even-length prefix is already valid; an odd-length prefix ends in `i` and needs one final `o`.
4. The scan only needs to remember the next expected character and the number of insertions.

## Solution sketch

1. “Every valid result is an even-length prefix of the infinite pattern `ioioio…`. Insertions preserve the order of the original characters, so the goal is to find the shortest such prefix containing `S` as a subsequence.” Read `S`, set the insertion count to zero, and start by expecting `i`.
2. “Matching each original character to its earliest available position leaves at least as much room for the remaining characters as any later match. In the alternating pattern, a match needs no insertion if the next expected character agrees, and exactly one insertion otherwise.” Scan `S` from left to right. On a mismatch, count one insertion of the expected character and switch the expectation. Then match the original character and switch the expectation again. This also handles a leading `o` and consecutive equal characters. Because each match is as early as possible, the last match cannot occur later than in any other embedding.
3. “After all original characters are matched, an even-length prefix is already valid; an odd-length prefix ends in `i` and needs one final `o`.” If the next expected character is `o`, add one to the count; otherwise, leave it unchanged. This rounds the last matched position up to the smallest even length, preserving optimality. An already valid string incurs no insertions. Print the count.
4. “The scan only needs to remember the next expected character and the number of insertions.” Each character takes constant time to process, so the algorithm runs in \(O(|S|)\) time and uses \(O(1)\) auxiliary space beyond the input string.
